newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt investors offer shares in new cement firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt investors offer shares in new cement firm.

text.p: Egyptian investors said on Friday they are offering the public nine million shares in a new cement company at 10.00 pounds ($3) each.
The offer in Egypt Cement (Qena) will remain open for a month from February 16, but it could be closed after a minimum of ten days if it is fully covered.
Investors can apply for 25 shares or more, with only a quarter of their value payable plus an issue fee of 0.10 pounds a share, the founders said in a published prospectus.
They said another 25 percent of the share value is to be paid within six months of the date of establishment. The company will ask for the remaining half within a year.
State-owned banks and insurance firms, including the National Bank of Egypt, the agent of the offer, hold at least 40 percent of the firm, which has a 300-million-pound paid up capital.
The expected annual return on capital would be 10 percent, they added.
The cement sector is highly profitable in Egypt and cement firms are among the stock market blue chips.
